## Part 2 — Excluded sources


### Celestial / Astrological (Enūma Anu Enlil)

| Museum no. / siglum | Period | Publication / edition | Reason for exclusion |
|---|---|---|---|
| KBo 8.6 | Middle Babylonian | KBo 8.6. CTH 532 (hethiter.net AOxml). Lunar-eclipse omens (Enūma Anu Enlil tradition) — the AKKADIAN column of an Akkadian–Hittite BILINGUAL; only the Akkadian side is given here (the Hittite translation is not in this AOxml). | Akkadian column of an Akk–Hitt bilingual — mention only, do not count. Its syllabic Akkadian (LDI ≈ 0.09) is a bilingual-transmission effect, so it would distort the monolingual astrology cell. |
| Rm 267 | Neo-Assyrian | eBL fragment Rm.267 (transliteration verbatim from electronic Babylonian Library) | Rochberg source subsumed in EAE20/RecA-RecB composites; held out to avoid double-count |
| Sm 246 | Neo-Assyrian | eBL fragment Sm.246 (transliteration verbatim from electronic Babylonian Library) | Rochberg source subsumed in EAE20/RecA-RecB composites; held out to avoid double-count |
| K 3561 | Neo-Babylonian | hand-transcribed from Rochberg's "Recension B Transliteration" partitur (the numbered reference line ≈ source S, with brackets where S is broken; restorations in §§ III and X–XII partly from sources U/T). Not in eBL. Determinatives normalized to {} to match the eBL-sourced files. | Rochberg source subsumed in EAE20/RecA-RecB composites; held out to avoid double-count |


### Terrestrial (Šumma Ālu)

| Museum no. / siglum | Period | Publication / edition | Reason for exclusion |

| Emar.VI.700 | Middle Babylonian | Arnaud 1987, Emar VI/4 no. 700 (Msk 74107k). "Présages tirés des bœufs" — cattle omens (Šumma Ālu animal-section adjacent). Western-periphery witness cited by Koch 2015 §4.5.2. | too fragmentary to count. Worth MENTIONING in the article: it scores LDI = 1.00, but only as a preservation artifact — the sole surviving signs are the all-logographic omen-skeleton (the broken protases BE GU₄.ḪI.A "if oxen…"); the (potentially syllabic) apodoses are lost. So the 1.00 measures what survives, not the omens. |
